Definition: fright; concrete, an idol (as a bugbear)
BiblicalUsage: ʼêymâh is a plain word for fright; concrete, an idol (as a bugbear). It appears in Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, and Joshua, and each time it carries that same plain sense. The word keeps that same sense wherever it appears.
TheologicalSignificance: What ʼêymâh teaches me is that fear is honest, but it is not the last word — God is bigger than what frightens us. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Call of Abraham; The Walls of Jericho
